# A/B Testing and Business Metrics

## Overview
A/B testing is how data-driven companies make decisions: instead of guessing whether a new button, price, or feature is better, they run a controlled experiment. Users are randomly split into a control group (current version, A) and a treatment group (new version, B), and you compare a chosen metric between them. This is the practical application of the hypothesis testing you learned: the null hypothesis is 'no difference,' and you use a statistical test to decide whether the observed difference is real or just chance. Good design comes first: you define one primary metric tied to a business goal (like conversion rate or revenue per user), and you calculate the required sample size in advance so the test has enough power to detect a meaningful effect. Connecting to business metrics is key, a data scientist must translate statistical results into business impact ('this change would lift revenue ~3%'). Beware common pitfalls: 'peeking' at results early and stopping when they look good inflates false positives, testing many metrics at once causes spurious findings, and short-term 'novelty effects' can mislead. A/B testing is one of the most valued and widely-used skills in industry data science.

## Deep Dive
This module covers: What A/B testing is and why companies use it; Designing an experiment (hypothesis, metric, sample size); Analyzing results with hypothesis testing; Key business metrics (conversion, retention, revenue); Pitfalls (peeking, multiple testing, novelty effect). Mastering these ideas is essential because they appear repeatedly in production AI systems.

### What You Will Learn
- The core theory behind today's topic.
- How to apply it using Python, NumPy, Pandas, or the relevant framework.
- How to evaluate results and avoid common mistakes.
- Where to find authoritative references when you need deeper detail.

### Real-World Context
In industry, these skills are used daily: data scientists clean messy survey data, AI engineers deploy models to REST APIs, and automation engineers orchestrate pipelines. Today's practical task simulates one of these real-world scenarios.

## Hands-On Practice
Practical Task: Design an A/B test for a hypothetical product change: state the hypothesis and primary metric, calculate the needed sample size, then simulate data and run the correct statistical test to reach a conclusion.
Mini Project: Analyze a real or simulated A/B test dataset end to end: check the setup, run the appropriate test, compute the effect size and confidence interval, and write a business-facing recommendation.
Assignment: Explain, with an example, why stopping an A/B test as soon as it looks significant ('peeking') leads to false positives.

Complete all three sections. Each completed section earns points toward your CalibiAI Score. If you are unsure about any part, use the AI assessment popup to submit your work and receive dynamic feedback from DeepSeek.

## Common Mistakes to Avoid
Many beginners rush into coding before fully understanding the data. Others skip validation steps and overestimate model performance. This module helps you build the discipline of checking assumptions first, then applying algorithms systematically.

## Career Impact
The skills covered today are frequently tested in technical interviews and required in entry-level AI engineering roles. Building a portfolio that demonstrates mastery of these concepts will significantly improve your job prospects.

## Key Takeaways
1. Theory guides practice — understand before coding.
2. Clean data and clear metrics are more valuable than complex models.
3. Document your steps for reproducibility.
4. Communication matters: explain results to non-technical stakeholders.
